title: SE For Free: Constructing Secondary Electron Images from Two-Channel STEM EBIC
content: Electron beam-induced current (EBIC) imaging associates the position of a focused electron beam with the current it generates in a sample. Depending on the current generation mechanism, EBIC images show contrast related to different electronic properties of the sample. The “standard” mode of EBIC measures current generated from separation of beam-induced electron-hole pairs (EHPs) in a local electric field. This EBIC mode, performed mostly in the scanning electron microscope (SEM), has been used to image electric field in semiconductor devices since the 1960’s [1]. A more recently demonstrated EBIC mode, secondary electron emission EBIC (SEEBIC), measures the much (∼1000×) smaller currents produced when secondary electrons (SEs) are emitted from the sample [2]. SEEBIC has only been observed in the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM), where it has been used to demonstrate high-resolution STEM SE imaging [3, 4] as well as work function [2], conductivity [5], and temperature mapping [6].
